full_judgment: 2. The respondent No. 2 Uttara Bank instituted Money Suit No.92 of 2003 on 30-4-03 against the petitioner and another for realisation of Taka 17,88,34,045 including interest as on 30-4-03 and prayed for a decree for the said sum against the defendants jointly and severally. The defendant Nos. 1, 3 and 4, who are the petitioners before this Court, filed written statement denying their liability and asserted that they had no liability in respect of the cheques endorsed by the Sonali Bank being good for payment. In the suit, issues were framed on 22-4-04 and ultimately, the suit was ready for peremptory hearing and after that several adjournments were made. Thereafter, on 14-8-04, the defendant Nos. 1, 3, 4 and 5, the present petitioners, filed an application under Order I, rule 10 read with section 51 of the Code of Civil Procedure for striking out their names from the plaint stating that the plaintiff brought the suit without complying with the provision of the Negotiable Instruments Act which has caused serious prejudice to the defendants and therefore, the names of the defendants are improperly joined in the plaint and their presence before the Court were not at all necessary in order to enable the Court effectually and completely to adjudicate upon and settle all questions involved in the suit. The learned judge of the Artha Rin Adalat after hearing the parties by impugned order dated 4-9-04 rejected the application. In rejecting the application, the Adalat, however, found that the matter must be scrutinised under section 126 of the Contract Act as the section deals with the contract of guarantee which means a contract to perform the promises or discharge the liability of a third person in case of his default, and in the instant case the defendant No. 2 gave a guarantee as to the cheques as good for payment. In the absence of any written contract it cannot be presumed that by such endorsement the Sonali Bank undertook the liability of the principal debtor and, as such, the defendants on the basis of their guarantee and for that reason found that the defendant Nos. 1, 3, 4 and 5 are necessary parties in the suit for resolving the dispute.
